description: The attack requires the ability to modify the model's weights, which may not be possible for closed-source models.
label: Access to model weights

description: The probability that an alert is successfully parsed to the defender(s), affecting partial observability. Tested at reduced probabilities of 0.75 and 0.9.
label: Alert success probability

canonical_name: Attacker cannot access agent or user device
description: The attacker does not directly interact with the agent interface and does not compromise external tools, browsers, or client devices.
label: Attacker cannot access agent or user device

description: The attacker knows the target application domain and can infer common user goals, but does not know the agent's internal policy, system prompt, or exact user request.
label: Attacker knows target application domain

description: The attacker keeps prior inputs, defender responses, and scorer feedback across rounds.
label: Attacker retains history and feedback

description: The attack is particularly effective on autoregressive models like GPT-J, Llama-2, and Llama-3.
label: Autoregressive base models

description: The base station is assumed to be secure and cannot be compromised by adversaries.
label: Base station is safe

description: Attacks performed without access to model parameters.
label: Black-box access

description: Artifact writes are permitted only under complete and only within the admissible boundary of the current task kind.
label: Boundary discipline

description: Each battle allows up to 15 rounds and stops at the first scored success.
label: Bounded rounds

description: A task must be claimed before work is performed; substantive work and file updates are forbidden while the task is in todo.
label: Claim-before-work

description: Once a task is in_progress and assigned to the same actor, the agent may emit complete with verification checks and bounded file updates.
label: Complete-after-work

canonical_name: Defender controls the user's personal LLM agent
description: The defender possesses full control over the design and implementation of the user’s personal LLM agent, including internal logic, prompts, policies, modules, and interaction protocols.
label: Defender controls the user's personal LLM agent

description: Once a task is terminal, it must not be silently reopened; corrections must route through explicit issue or hotfix flows.
label: Done immutability

description: Financial LLM agents have direct execution authority over real capital, making actions financially irreversible.
label: Execution authority over real capital

description: The defender receives no prior-round history, modeling a fresh session for each attempt.
label: Fresh-session defender

description: Injected prompts are non-obvious to human observers (low contrast, small font).
label: Human-imperceptible prompts

description: Each node has three types of keys: Node Based Keys, Pair Wise Keys, and Broadcast Keys.
label: Key types

description: Completion is valid only when the current actor owns the task.
label: Lock ownership

description: Once harmful content is uploaded, it persists indefinitely and can be ingested by web crawlers for future training datasets.
label: Misinformation persists in digital ecosystem

canonical_name: No direct access to model weights
description: The data-poisoning attack does not require direct access to model weights; it relies on uploading misinformation to the Internet.
label: No direct access to model weights

description: The frontier scaffold executes no external tools or actions; success checks measure output violations only.
label: No external tools or actions

description: Each node is identified by a Group ID (8 bits) and Node ID (8 bits), limiting communication to the group.
label: Node identification

description: There is a nonzero probability of delivering messages to related destinations.
label: Nonzero probability of message delivery

description: Each defensive agent has its own view of the network state, and knowledge is not shared among agents.
label: Partial observability

description: The agent must restate the status it believes it is operating under, allowing the orchestrator to reject stale-context or out-of-phase execution attempts.
label: Prior-status consistency

description: One agent's output instantly becomes another's input, creating reflexive dynamics that can amplify cascades.
label: Reflexive market

description: Time Division Multiplexing is used for communication within a group, allowing nodes to listen passively in promiscuous mode.
label: TDM scheduling within groups

description: The user query is considered trusted and is used for abstract plan generation.
label: Trusted user query

description: Third-party apps are considered untrusted and may be malicious.
label: Untrusted apps

canonical_name: User's personal agent and direct input queries are benign
description: The defender operates under the assumption that the user’s personal LLM agent and direct input queries are intrinsically benign.
label: User's personal agent and direct input queries are benign

description: Adversaries are directly profit-motivated, and the market is zero-sum, so attacks can be financially incentivized.
label: Zero-sum adversarial market
